subject: Random Walk Precision Matrix: what does INLA output?

messages.author: 2f6c5eed34f4bc17
messages.subject: Random Walk Precision Matrix: what does INLA output?
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to understand what quantity INLA outputs in the random-effects block of the precision matrix for a RW1 model. I have the following tiny example:

```r
n <- 5
set.seed(79687)
u <- runif(n) # Covariates to be modelled smoothly
eta <- cos(u) + rnorm(n,0,exp(-12))
y <- rnorm(n,eta,.1)

df <- tibble(y = y,u = u)

inlaiid <- inla(
  y ~ 1 + f(u,model = "iid",initial = 0,fixed = TRUE)
  data = df,
  family = "gaussian",
  control.family = list(initial = 0,fixed = TRUE),
  control.inla = list(strategy='gaussian',int.strategy = "eb",correct = FALSE),
  control.compute=list(config=TRUE),
  control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE,initial = 0,fixed = TRUE),
  control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0,mean.intercept = 0)
)

inla_Q <- forceSymmetric(inlaiid$misc$config$config[[1]]$Q,'U')
inla_Q
```

I am able to manually reproduce the contents of inla_Q for this IID model. I set all precisions to 1 (i.e. log-precisions to 0) just to make the output easier to read, I know this is not the proper way to approach this if this were a real problem.

When running the same thing for a RW1 model on the random effect, I notice two things that confuse me:
1) The "linear predictor" and "fixed effects" blocks of inla_Q are understandable to me (given the math I have worked out); the "random effects" block (indices 6 - 10 in my concrete example) contains numbers I completely can't reproduce, and
2) When I run the model with the default sum-to-zero constraint, and when I run it with the first coordinate constrained to be zero and no sum-to-zero constraint, I get the same inla_Q matrix.

II would really appreciate anyone helping to clear up: what quantity does misc$config$config[[1]]$Q contain in this situation? Is it the rank-deficient RW1 precision matrix, or the full-rank matrix obtained by applying the linear constraint? The output has full dimension and full rank, so I am pretty confused by this. I have read chapter 3 of Rue and Held (2005) and still don't understand.

Code for RW1:

```r 
inlarw1 <- inla(
  y ~ 1 + f(u,model = "iid",initial = 0,fixed = TRUE),
  data = df,
  family = "gaussian",
  control.family = list(initial = 0,fixed = TRUE),
  control.inla = list(strategy='gaussian',int.strategy = "eb",correct = FALSE),
  control.compute=list(config=TRUE),
  control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE,initial = 0,fixed = TRUE),
  control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0,mean.intercept = 0)
)
```

Code for RW1 with manual constraint:

```r
# Constraints
constr_A <- matrix(c(1,rep(0,n-1)),nrow = 1)
constr_e <- rep(0,nrow(constr_A))

# Fit INLA
inlarw1constr <- inla(
  y ~ 1 + f(u,model = "iid",initial = 0,fixed = TRUE,constr = FALSE,extraconstr = list(A = constr_A,e = constr_e)),
  data = df,
  family = "gaussian",
  control.family = list(initial = 0,fixed = TRUE),
  control.inla = list(strategy='gaussian',int.strategy = "eb",correct = FALSE),
  control.compute=list(config=TRUE),
  control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE,initial = 0,fixed = TRUE),
  control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0,mean.intercept = 0)
)
```

Thank you in advance to anyone who takes the time to read this and offer advice!

Alex

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random Walk Precision Matrix: what does INLA output?
parts:
Hi,

these computations are spelled out here

Article{art632,
author = {H. Rue and A. Riebler and S. H. S{\o}rbye and J. B.
Illian and D. P. Simpson and F. K. Lindgren},
title = {Bayesian Computing with {INLA}: {A} Review},
journal = {Annual Reviews of Statistics and Its Applications},
keywords = {year2017,my.own,my.cv},
year = 2017,
volume = 4,
number = {March},
pages = {395--421},
doi = {10.1146/annurev-statistics-060116-054045}
}

or check the arxiv version.

The constraints are not part of the precision matrix, as they are used
to correct the mean/variance, as describer in the GMRF book section
2.3.3


If its still unclear, let me know

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random Walk Precision Matrix: what does INLA output?
parts:
Thanks! Those calculations match what I have so that's very encouraging. What I am confused about are the dimension and rank of A and Q for a random walk 1. If your f_1 term has a RW1 model, then m1 = n, but my understanding is that rank(A) = rank(Q) = n-1, and one linear constraint is needed. From the GMRF book, I understand that computations can proceed using such a singular precision matrix, with determinants being taken as the product of only the non-zero eigenvalues etc, and then (as you say) the mean and variance are corrected at the end only, using available formulas.

This would all make sense to me, but when I run the RW1 model as initially posted, with inla_Q as the output of misc$config$config[[1]]$Q, I get
> dim(inla_Q)
[1] 11 11
> rankMatrix(inla_Q)
[1] 11

n = 5 so this dimension corresponds to 5 nodes in the latent field, 5 random effects (random walk evaluations), and the intercept, which makes sense. But why is it full rank? Does INLA do something here that is documented elsewhere, or am I misunderstanding the basic theory? My understanding of your previous response is that this should actually be rank 10.

Really appreciate you taking the time!

Alex
